about: Lab PR 246 over lab PR 244: a program staged in /tmp connects to a network canary on a loopback port nothing listens on; the close of the refused socket reaches the engine before the trip (judged as any flow, before any precursor, and noted as an egress), then the trip, then the program's exec record, processed last though it came first in kernel time. NN-L-CHAIN-002's late exec (lab PR 244) would complete the chain with the trip's own connection; the trip dropped that note, so the late exec is R001's alone. A later flow of the program is NN-L-CHAIN-002 and NN-L-CHAIN-003.

decision.name: Canary network connect
decision.reasoning: Network canary connected — zero-FP intrusion signal; kill the accessor tree + posture → COMBAT

decision.name: Exec from /tmp/
decision.reasoning: Process executed from /tmp/ — common malware staging location

decision.name: /tmp exec followed by network egress
decision.reasoning: Process executed from a staging directory (/tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm) then opened an outbound flow (other than a lookup at a configured resolver) within the correlation window — dropper C2 (T1059 → T1571); kill the process tree + posture → COMBAT [also matched: NN-L-CHAIN-003_CanaryThenEgress (KillProcessTree, Critical), NN-L-NET-008_OutboundFromTmpExec (KillProcess, High)]
